title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court Concerning the Entrusted Agents of Victims in Public Prosecution Cases and the Litigation Rights They Shall Enjoy

articles.content_en: I. According to the provisions of Article 2, Item (3) of the Interim Regulations on Lawyers, the lawyer's practice includes accepting the entrustment of "the victim of a public prosecution case and his/her near relatives to act as agent and participate in the proceedings." Therefore, where the victim of a public prosecution case has not died, the People's Court shall permit the victim to entrust a lawyer to act as agent and participate in the proceedings; if the victim has not entrusted a lawyer, his/her near relatives may also entrust a lawyer to act as agent with the consent of the victim. Where the victim of a public prosecution case has died, in order to fully protect the lawful rights and interests of the victim, the People's Court shall also permit the near relatives of the victim to entrust a lawyer to act as agent and participate in the proceedings.

II. Where a lawyer acts as agent for the victim of a public prosecution case, the litigation rights enjoyed by the lawyer shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law, the Interim Regulations on Lawyers, the "Joint Notice on Several Specific Provisions Concerning Lawyers' Participation in Litigation" issued by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice [(81) Fa Yan Zi No. 6] and the "Several Supplementary Provisions on Lawyers' Participation in Litigation" [(86) Si Fa Gong Zi No. 196], that is: the lawyer may go to the court to consult the materials of the case and understand the facts of the case; during the trial, with the permission of the presiding judge, the lawyer may ask questions and answer questions during the court investigation, state the opinions of the client to the court, participate in the debate, and express opinions on the handling of the case, etc.
January 22, 1992
